subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm scoping a manageable but detailed design: a heavy six-wheeled armored hauler with a cab, armor plating, a turret, and a sealed cargo pod featuring glowing seams and neon decals, built as a static model using basic geometric shapes rather than a rigged creature.

I'm planning out dimensions, helper functions for boxes and cylinders, a dark gunmetal and magenta/cyan color palette, and SVG textures for hazard stripes and a "SEALED" pod emblem.

Now I'm detailing the chassis structure, multiple wheel axles with cyan-lit hubs, and armored fenders before moving into the cab geometry.

Writing cab extrusion shape...

Working out the windshield tilt angle, around -12 degrees, matching the slope between the two reference points. I'll use a slightly offset plane with the glass texture, positioned forward along the normal from the windshield's center point.

Now mapping out side windows facing left and right at the cab's midpoint height, plus hood details -- a front bumper with armor styling and hazard stripe texture, and a grille plane with an LED glow effect positioned on the hood's front face.

Repositioning headlights near the grille and adding a glowing light bar on the roof. I'm also planning a remote weapon turret on the cab roof with twin barrels and a red sensor dome, plus side shield plates, before moving to the exposed chassis behind the cab leading into the flatbed pod.

For the pod itself, I'm sketching an octagonal prism along the z-axis using a low-segment cylinder geometry, sized to sit on cradles above the chassis and rotated so a flat face points upward for that low-poly cyberpunk look.

Adding ribs as thin raised octagon bands at intervals with glowing dark seams, then placing an emblem on the rear face for the main view and side decals on the flat faces at the octagon's apothem distance.

I'm adding diagonal glowing cyan strips rotated 45° along the pod's diagonal faces, then sizing the pod's overall width and vertical center so I can position cradle support blocks correctly against the chassis top.

For the gap between the cab and pod, I'm adding pressurized connector hoses with a magenta glow sweeping between the cab's rear wall and the pod's front. Then I'm working out armored side skirts to cover the wheel arches, figuring out their x-position based on the wheel width and the chassis and cab widths.

Now I'm placing the axle positions along the z-axis, settling on front and rear tandem pairs around 3.3/1.9 and -2.3/-3.7, while checking that the wheel radius doesn't clip through the cab floor height.

Checking wheel positioning against the cab, I notice the wheels at x=1.1-1.6 would intrude into the cab body at ±1.35, so I'm shifting wheel centers out to x=±1.65 to clear both cab and pod widths, landing on a total vehicle width near 3.85 — a chunky, wide convoy-style hauler.

Now I'm adding fenders over each wheel with box-shaped armor plates and side guards, positioning them around the wheel tops at y≈1.5, plus mud flaps near the front wheel at z≈3.3 within the cab's lower body span. For the wheels themselves I'm defining octagonal tire cylinders in dark tones, grey rims, and a glowing cyan hub ring...

Each wheel assembly needs a handful of lug bolts (I'll cap it at five per wheel to keep part counts reasonable across eight wheels), plus steel axle rods connecting left and right sides and differential boxes at the axle centers, with the chassis underside set at y=0.5 so it clears the wheels sitting at ground level. I'm also planning angular side armor plates for the cab to give it a more military look.

Writing extrude geometry...

Attaching the stacks to the cab with glow tips and caps for a good silhouette, then moving to the rear end: bumper, glowing tail lights, pod emblem, and hitch positioned near the chassis tail. I'm also adding a bulkhead to connect the pod front to the cab, and designing a roof turret with a ring base, box body, and twin barrels extending forward along the z-axis.

Positioning the sensor eye as a glowing red sphere and confirming the turret sits properly within the roof bounds. I'm also planning thin antenna rods with glow tips on the pod rear, plus a row of small cyan glowing boxes along the pod's top ridge to simulate dashed lights.

For the rear pod end, I'm working out an octagonal cap with a textured "sealed door" face showing a hex lock and chevrons, making sure the plane's orientation and up-vector are set so the texture reads correctly when viewed from outside the pod.

Now I'm adding neon underglow strips along the chassis skirts in magenta, plus side skirt panels between the wheel axles and hanging fuel tank cylinders positioned along the body sides.

I'm also sketching in reactive armour tiles on the pod's lower side faces, laying out a grid of small plate boxes for that detailed panelling effect.

Let me settle on five bands at z=1.15, -0.2, -1.5, -2.8, -4.15 with roughly 1.3 spacing, leaving gaps of about 1.0 for tiles between them—eight tiles total across both sides, with one tile reserved for a decal label near the middle.

For the tile texture I'm designing a custom "plate" paint with grime noise and edge lines to simulate riveted metal, skipping floor lights and ensuring mud flaps clear the ground above the tires. I'm adding side mirror arms with small glowing indicator boxes, skipping wipers and cab steps, and sketching a front bull bar with a wedge-shaped plow blade extruded in the x-z plane ahead of the bumper.

I'm defining the bumper as an octagon-ish plan shape with chamfered corners, positioning it between the cab front and headlights, and adding a hazard texture plane centered on its front face.

Now I'm setting up the paint system: a gunmetal countershaded hull paint using noise and smoothstep for grime and dirt gradients, plus an accent color palette (magenta, cyan, yellow, red) and a texture list covering hazard stripes, a glowing grille with cyan LED chevrons, and a windshield material.

I'm sketching out the remaining textures: tinted glass panels with reflection streaks and HUD lines, dark side windows, a glowing hex-locked pod rear door, a sealed pod label with trefoil icon and serial text, a door tag reading "CONVOY 07" (avoiding CJK characters), a tail light with slit detailing, and a circuit-pattern trim for the cab's roof panels -- about eight textures total, with text rendered using a monospace or sans font.

Now I'm working through the glow logic for textured parts like the grille, making sure the windshield stays glow-free, and reasoning through how single-sided planes on the pod's left and right faces should orient outward so labels stay readable from both viewing angles given the forward and up vectors.

Writing helper function...

I'm reconsidering the rig structure—since no joints are strictly required for static parts, maybe I should still create a root "chassis" joint and separate wheel joints so the wheels can spin independently.

Setting up wheel joints with naming...

Adding hub cap and lug nuts arranged in a ring using trig for positioning, with dark tire paint and a lighter metallic rim color, then moving on to connecting axle rods...

Still designing chassis...

Working out the octagon geometry for the pod extrusion, computing apothem-based vertices and centering the thickness along the z-axis. Now checking the reinforcement bands' scaled outline against wheel clearance to make sure the wheel positions don't collide with the band width at the relevant heights.

Writing paint function...

Now I'm placing the rear door frame and plane geometry, working out the exact z-offsets so the frame and end cap sit flush against the pod's rear face without clipping.

I'm positioning the rear bumper box and tail light glow elements near the chassis end, then starting to lay out the cab profile points for extrusion.

Still writing cab shape...

Adding a tilted visor box near the windshield top, then placing an alternating magenta-cyan light bar above it, and positioning the turret base on top of the roof armor.

Checking that the barrel start lines up with the turret body edge at z 2.9, then adding roof whip antennas with glowing tips, plus mirror arms extending from the cab sides to small glowing mirror boxes. I'm also planning side armor plates on the cab.

Working out the armor plate position so it clears the wheel well, then placing a neon door tag reading "C-07" on the plate's outer face.

Side window planes go at x ±1.303, sized 0.85x0.6, checking they stay within the cab's sloped front boundary at various heights. No rear bulkhead needed, but I'm now noticing the exhaust stack placement at x ±1.5 might clash with the fender geometry, so I need to resolve that overlap.

Positioning the exhaust stacks rising from the fender top at x ±1.5, z ~1.92, radius .11, height from y 1.5 to 3.6, with a flared glowing tip and bracket boxes connecting to the cab. Then defining fenders as boxes roughly 0.8 wide by 0.1 tall by 1.7 deep positioned over each wheel.

Adding fender arch lips and magenta edge glow stripes, totaling 24 fender parts across 8 wheels times 3 pieces each. I'm reconsidering the rear tandem wheels since their 1.4 spacing means individual 1.7-length fenders would overlap, so I'm adjusting toward individual 1.4-length fenders sized to the wheel diameter for a cleaner tandem fit.

Now adding mudflaps behind the rear wheels and placing cylindrical fuel tanks in the gap between the front and rear wheel positions along the chassis, figuring out their length and mounting height with strap-style brackets.

Modeling the tanks as capsule geometries oriented along the vehicle's length so they get rounded ends, with a few band boxes for detailing. Now I'm adding glow strips under the frame edges for an underside neon effect.

Working out armor pod tile positions along the side faces, placing them in the gaps between the body bands so they sit flush against the surface.

I also need matching tile rows on the top face, plus small label decals on specific tiles for the "SEALED" tag, while leaving the rest plain-painted with a subtle rivet pattern tied to the geometry's UV coordinates.

For positioning, I'm working out exact tile boundaries so labels sit flush against the tile face, and figuring out the diagonal strip placement around the pod by rotating boxes to the four 45-degree offset angles at a fixed radius from the axis.

Still planning geometry details...

Now I'm adding sagging coupling hoses between the cab and pod with magenta glowing cores and dark sheaths, plus connector details at the joints.

I realize I need to explicitly pass `bone: chassis` to every part call since unrooted pieces default to the nearest joint, which could wrongly attach decor to wheel joints instead — so I'll build helper wrapper functions that default to the chassis bone for all sweeps and parts.

Now I'm positioning the rear pod details: antennas at the rear deck corners with glowing cyan tips, hose sweeps, and a rear ladder with rail rods.

I'm placing the windshield plane with a backward tilt, calculating its size and offset so it aligns with the sloped frame line.

Designing more texture SVGs...

For the label, I'm drawing a dark hazard panel with yellow border, trefoil icon, "SEALED" text, and barcode lines, kept non-glowing. Then I'm adding a DOORTAG with neon cyan "C-07" text that glows, and a TAIL piece with glowing red slits. For the circuit trim texture, I'm figuring out placement—deciding to apply it to the outward-facing side skirt panels rather than the hood or cab sides.

I'm now second-guessing the circuit decal placement since skirts are occupied by tanks; considering roof pod bands or the front pod cap instead, but those extrude surfaces may not support textures well, so I'm weighing whether to just skip the circuit texture altogether given I already have nine or ten other textures in place (hazard, grille, wind, sidewin, reardoor, rearglow, label, doortag, tail).

I'm defining a hull paint function that uses noise to mix two base colors, brightens upward-facing normals with a bluish tint, adds dark grime near the bottom, and includes scratch lines, then I'm working through adding panel seam lines on the cab sides using modular arithmetic on the z-position to create periodic dark seams.

Now I'm picking specific colors for the cab and pod, adding magenta accent stripes and glowing bands along the cab's lower edge, plus yellow hazard striping on the bumper to tie into an overall neon caution-themed color scheme.

Setting flat shading on all geometry to avoid unnatural smooth shading on cylinder sides, then starting the actual build function with imports from the SDK and glow kit.

I'm defining a chassis joint for the convoy hauler, then creating small helper functions for placing boxes and cylinders onto that chassis bone with consistent flat shading...

Writing helper functions...

Defining rod and extrude helpers...

Still writing wheel assembly...

Adding a sidewall ring layer and checking depth ordering so tire, ring, and rim faces don't z-fight, then moving to the chassis joint and turret yaw/gun joint setup.

Now I'm working out positions for the headlights and grille relative to the hood front, checking embed depth and width so they sit flush against the cab face.

I need to tilt the grille plane by about 7° around the X axis to match the hood slope, applying the same correction to the headlights, then work out the bumper wedge geometry with its extrusion axes and thickness.

With the outline points set, I'm figuring out the bumper's front face position and checking that the hazard light plane fits within its flat section, then verifying the bumper height doesn't clash with the cab's lower front face or the front wheel position.

Still placing fender and light details...

Now I'm working out the deck, frame, and rear bumper box dimensions, checking that each piece's z-span and y-offset align without clipping the cab or front bumper.

Placing the tail light decals and planning a hazard stripe centered between them on the rear bumper...

Now sketching rear mudflap boxes positioned near the back wheel, and laying out hose sweep curves between the cab gaps with alternating colors.

Writing hose and tank code...

Checking tank placement against the wheel zones and frame edges to make sure the capsule and bracket boxes don't overlap the wheels or deck.

Now I'm positioning the roof lightbar as alternating magenta and cyan boxes mounted just above the roof line, and starting to place the turret.

For the turret base, I'm extruding octagonal bands with a dark fill color, then adding a magenta glow strip as a thin box along the top edge of the band to give it a subtle highlight.

Now I'm positioning five pod bands near the ends and placing plate-colored top tiles with a dome accent on one tile. I'm distributing side tiles across the pod's length and figuring out which ones should carry decals like hazard markings or labels.

I'm sizing an ID tag plane and a label plane with proper aspect ratios, deciding placement for readable text on the left-facing side. Now I'm writing SVG code to generate hazard stripe textures...

Still writing SVG textures...

Still writing HUD elements...

Writing SVG label markup...

Writing plate paint shader...

Checking plate placement near the wheel for overlap, then verifying the turret's total height against antenna and dome positions to confirm it stays proportional for a large hauler. I'm also double-checking the turret base cylinder sits correctly against the roof without clipping.

Now I'm sketching out the dish lathe profile and tilt axis for the satellite-style sensor on top, making sure the polygon outline stays non-self-intersecting before finalizing the rod and sweep helper calls.

Adding glowing sphere tips to the antenna, then writing the final code with loose `any` typing for color params to keep things simple.
